description: VECTOR_AVG - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. It averages ELEMENT-WISE and divides by the NON-NULL count, so a NULL row is skipped rather than counted as a zero vector. The mean elements are narrowed to float32: over [1,9,3], [4,5,-6] and [7,2,0] the middle element is 16/3 computed in float64 and then narrowed to 5.3333335, which a VECTOR cell renders with six decimals as 5.333333. It is the one vector aggregate that ALWAYS widens INT to FLOAT. An empty or all-NULL group is NULL, a single-row group is that row, and a non-vector argument is the compile error 'Invalid argument types for function VECTOR_AVG: (NUMBER(1,0))'. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorAvgTest (now retired); every vector is read as a bare cell, rendered as live's JDBC and REST render it - FLOAT elements with six decimals ([2.500000,3.500000,4.500000]), INT elements plain - because TO_VARCHAR over a VECTOR is refused on a real account.
